title: Create form locks every field whose readonlyWhen is TRUE against the field defaults, though the server exempts INSERT from readonlyWhen
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect with a reproduction (reach: console create form, measured once in the browser on 18.0.0).
Reader: objectui form renderer seat (`packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`, the per-field `resolveFieldRuleState` call), the next PR that touches create-mode rule evaluation.
Duplicate check: searched objectstack and objectui issues (open and closed) for "create form readonlyWhen evaluated on insert / fields read-only on new record": 6 + 12 hits, none about this (closest: objectui#12082, which was about permission grants, not `readonlyWhen`).

## What happens

A field whose `readonlyWhen` reads a column that has a `defaultValue` is shown read-only on the **create** form, because the form evaluates the predicate against the seeded defaults. The server, by contrast, does not apply `readonlyWhen` on INSERT (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, the insert-strip note: "What INSERT still does NOT strip: `readonlyWhen`"; objectui's own `form.tsx` comment says "objectql exempts INSERT from `readonlyWhen` entirely"). So the client is stricter than the server and the user cannot fill a form the API accepts.

## Reproduction (hotsrm, platform 18.0.0)

```ts
const locked = P`record.status == 'pending_verify' || record.status == 'active'`;
status: Field.select({ defaultValue: 'pending_verify', readonly: true, options: [...] }),
bank_name: Field.text({ required: true, readonlyWhen: locked }),
account_no: Field.text({ required: true, readonlyWhen: locked }),
```

1. Open the object's list in the console and click New.
2. Every field with `readonlyWhen: locked` renders as a read-only `—`; the dialog has no inputs except the boolean toggle, and Create can only fail on the required fields.
3. `POST /api/v1/data/<object>` with the same fields as the same user succeeds (201, the values are stored).

Same with a predicate over an unset field: `readonlyWhen: P\`record.approval_status != 'returned'\`` locks the whole create form, because `null != 'returned'` is TRUE.

## Expected

On a create form (no `previousValues`, the same `isCreateForm` signal the readonly strip already uses), `readonlyWhen` should not lock the field, matching the server. If locking on create is intended, the server should enforce it on INSERT too, and the spec text for `Field.readonlyWhen` should say so; either way client and server should agree.

## Workaround in the app

Guard the predicate with `has(record.id) && record.id != null && (...)`; the stored row on UPDATE carries `id`, the create form does not.
